text:
Adrian Kempe's week went from a high-stick on Dakota Joshua to the shootout winner against Toronto, and then a fine from the NHL for the high-stick, as NDTV Sports put it in one headline. Off the scoresheet, the bigger question for the Kings is why a player getting this many looks has only six goals.

He has 59 shots and 9.44 expected goals, so six goals is a shortfall of about three and a half, and Los Angeles has also scored 6.8 fewer goals than expected with him on. Both tend to swing back. The underlying play is excellent: the Kings take 58.1% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him, almost 12 points better than without him. Three of his goals came in one night against San Jose.

The usual caveat with Kempe is on the other side of the puck. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.18 more expected goals per 60 with him on in 2025-26 (bottom 5% of forwards), and penalties cost him 3.2 goals. This season's five-on-five numbers look much better. Our numbers project 66 points and 30 goals, with a range of 24 to 38 goals.
headline: Kempe's week: a fine, a shootout winner, few goals
